title: Case: Two of five insured cartons of ceramics outstanding six weeks after a cross-city shipment
context: A potter sent five insured cartons across the city through a freight broker, with Hartwold Arc as carrier. Three were delivered. The insurance was placed through the broker.
initial_request: SIX WEEK. I send 5 carton, 3 arrive, 2 is gone, and I pay insurance for all 5!! Broker tell me ask Hartwold. Hartwold tell me ask broker. Now broker say again wait for Hartwold. Who is lying to me?? This is 2 carton of my glazed bowls, 3 month of my work from the kiln, I am one person studio not big company. My customer is waiting and I must pay them back from my own pocket. Do NOT write me again 'your claim is in progress'. In progress WHERE. Tell me is it LOST or is it BROKEN and WHEN I get the answer.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Hartwold Arc Logistics
events.body: Trace TR-8250 for DL-5263 (5 cartons). Cartons 1, 2 and 5 delivered 11 January. Cartons 3 and 4: no scan after the collection scan on 10 January. Not located. Recorded as lost in transit.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Niamh Whitlock, shipper
events.body: The insurance on DL-5263 was placed through us. The insurer assesses on the carrier's written finding for each carton: either lost, or damaged with an inspection report. We have seen a trace note saying lost but no formal finding. Please get one from Hartwold Arc.

DL-5263, cartons 3 and 4 of 5. The shipper's insurance was placed through her broker, Cask & Tiller Freight, and the insurer needs Hartwold Arc's written finding for each carton. Trace TR-8250 records them as lost in transit. Please issue the formal finding.
The insurance on DL-5263 is the broker's policy, not ours. The claim sits with Cask & Tiller. Please refer the shipper to them.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Niamh Whitlock, shipper
events.body: Still no finding from Hartwold Arc on DL-5263 cartons 3 and 4. We cannot file with the insurer until the carrier states in writing whether each carton is lost or damaged. The insurer closes unactioned notifications at 60 days, which is 25 March.

Housekeeping query. The damages cage holds 2 cartons labelled DL-5263 3/5 and 4/5, logged in on 11 January as 'crushed, contents rattling'. No claim or disposal instruction is attached to them. The cage is cleared on 26 February and anything without an instruction is disposed of.

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the trace record (lost) and the depot record (two cartons in the damages cage) to Delivery investigations and ask for a written finding per carton, with the cartons kept from disposal meanwhile.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Hartwold Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the Parcel trace team to reconcile TR-8250 with the depot's record of cartons 3/5 and 4/5 in the damages cage and state in writing which is correct, with the cartons kept from disposal meanwhile.

Answer the depot's housekeeping query: ask it to keep cartons 3/5 and 4/5 out of the 26 February clearance until Delivery investigations instruct, because the trace records them as lost and the carrier's written finding is still owed.

must: Sets out both records as a contradiction the carrier still has to resolve: trace TR-8250 says cartons 3 and 4 were never scanned after collection and are lost, while the Destination depot says two cartons labelled DL-5263 3/5 and 4/5 have been in its damages cage since 11 January.

Asks that the two cartons are not disposed of in the 26 February cage clearance, and states that the carrier's written finding for each carton (lost, or damaged with an inspection report) is what is needed and has not been issued.

Tells the team what depends on it for the shipper so they prioritise: her insurance claim has been stuck since January because it cannot be filed without the carrier's finding and the insurer closes the notification on 25 March. Asks for a confirmation or a date the desk can pass on to her.
must_not: Tells Niamh as fact that the cartons are lost, or that they have been found, or that the contents are broken.
Tells Niamh the claim is in progress, or is being looked into, without naming who is settling what and by when.
Refers her back to the broker, or tells her the matter is the broker's and not the carrier's.
Promises an insurance payout, compensation or return of the cartons.
Gives the Destination depot an instruction to dispose of, release or forward the two cartons.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: DL-5263, cartons 3 and 4 of 5, shipper Niamh Whitlock. Two Hartwold Arc records now disagree and I need you to establish which is right. Trace TR-8250 (18 January) says cartons 3 and 4 had no scan after collection on 10 January and records them as lost in transit. This morning the Destination depot told me its damages cage holds two cartons labelled DL-5263 3/5 and 4/5, logged in on 11 January as crushed with contents rattling, with no claim or instruction attached. I am not assuming either record is correct. Please confirm what those two cartons are and issue a written finding for each carton, lost or damaged with an inspection report. I understand the policy is the broker's, but their insurer will only assess on the carrier's written finding, and it closes the notification on 25 March. The depot clears the cage on 26 February, so please make sure nothing labelled DL-5263 is disposed of before your finding. The shipper has been sent between Hartwold Arc and Cask & Tiller for six weeks. She is a one-person pottery studio, the two cartons are about three months of her work, and she is repaying her own customer in the meantime. Please give me a date for the finding that I can pass on to her.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2109: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
